summary: Adds new IP Flow Information Export (IPFIX) code points that show which MPLS control protocol was used to forward traffic in a Segment Routing domain. It defines five values for the mplsTopLabelType element, covering PCE, IS-IS, OSPFv2, OSPFv3, and BGP. This helps operators understand their traffic flows. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Traffic gets a label showing which road map was used. Now monitoring tools can tell which map the traffic followed.

questions: ipfix mpls segment routing label type
how to tell which protocol allocated a segment routing label
what are the five code points in rfc 9160
how to identify which protocol allocated an mpls label
subtitle: New IPFIX code points to identify which routing protocol allocated an MPLS Segment Routing label.

tldr.problem: Network operators can see MPLS labels flowing through their networks but cannot tell which control plane protocol (PCE, IS-IS, OSPF, BGP) allocated each label, because different protocols may use overlapping label ranges.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9160 adds five new code points to the IPFIX mplsTopLabelType information element to identify labels allocated by Path Computation Element, IS-IS, OSPFv2, OSPFv3, and BGP Segment Routing.
tldr.outcome: Operators can now monitor protocol migrations and understand traffic flow routing, for example when upgrading from LDP to IS-IS or OSPF Segment Routing.

today: RFC 9160 is an informational RFC published in December 2021. The code points have been registered with IANA and are available for use by IPFIX implementations that need to report on Segment Routing deployments.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content:
Segment Routing simplifies MPLS by having routers insert labels based on path computation. Five control plane protocols can allocate these labels: PCE (Path Computation Element), IS-IS, OSPFv2, OSPFv3, and BGP.

IPFIX (IP Flow Information Export) can report which traffic uses which label. However, the existing mplsTopLabelType element could not distinguish between different Segment Routing protocols because the RFC did not define code points for them. Different protocols may allocate labels in overlapping ranges, making manual identification impossible.
sections.eli5: Network operators can see labels on traffic but do not know which routing protocol created them. This makes it hard to track what is happening during network migrations.

sections.title: The Solution
sections.content:
RFC 9160 defines five new code points for the IPFIX mplsTopLabelType(46) information element:

Code point 6 for Path Computation Element (PCE), code point 7 for OSPFv2 Segment Routing, code point 8 for OSPFv3 Segment Routing, code point 9 for IS-IS Segment Routing, and code point 10 for BGP Prefix-SID. These values are registered with IANA in the IPFIX MPLS label type subregistry.

When traffic flows through a network, IPFIX now reports which of these five protocols allocated the top label in the MPLS label stack.
sections.eli5: Now every monitored traffic flow can report which of the five protocols created its label, making it clear which control plane is being used.

sections.title: Use Cases
sections.content:
Two main use cases are addressed: monitoring MPLS control plane migrations from LDP (Label Distribution Protocol) to Segment Routing variants like IS-IS or OSPF, and monitoring migrations from dynamic BGP labels to BGP Segment Routing Prefix-SIDs.

Operators can use the new code points together with other IPFIX elements (mplsTopLabelIPv4Address, mplsTopLabelStackSection, and forwardingStatus) to understand packet forwarding, drops, and the provider edge addresses involved. This visibility is critical during gradual protocol migrations, where different parts of the network may use different routing protocols.
sections.eli5: Operators doing a gradual upgrade can see exactly which parts of their network have switched to the new protocol and verify that traffic is flowing correctly through both old and new systems.
